plan.title: Revenue growth by region, 2022 to 2025
plan.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT region, year(order_date) AS yr, sum(revenue) AS revenue
  FROM global_sales
  WHERE year(order_date) IN (2022, 2025)
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT region,
       round(sum(revenue) FILTER (WHERE yr = 2022), 2) AS revenue_2022,
       round(sum(revenue) FILTER (WHERE yr = 2025), 2) AS revenue_2025,
       round((revenue_2025 - revenue_2022) / revenue_2022, 4) AS growth_pct
FROM yearly
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY growth_pct DESC
plan.explanation: Adds up each region's revenue in 2022 and in 2025, then compares the two years. Regions are ranked by how much their revenue grew.
assumptions: Growth compares total revenue in 2022 (the first full year in the data) with 2025 (the last).
growth_pct is a fraction: 0.5 means revenue grew by 50%.

question: What is total revenue by year?

plan.title: Total revenue by year
plan.sql:
SELECT year(order_date) AS year, round(sum(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM global_sales
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY year
plan.explanation: Adds up the revenue of every order, grouped by the year the order was placed.
assumptions: Revenue is net of discounts, as stored in the revenue column.

question: Show the monthly revenue trend by channel

plan.title: Monthly revenue by channel
plan.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS month, channel, round(sum(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM global_sales
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY month, channel
plan.explanation: Adds up revenue for each month and sales channel, so the channels can be compared over time.
assumptions: Months are calendar months of the order date.

plan.title: Top 10 products by revenue, 2025
plan.sql:
SELECT product, round(sum(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM global_sales
WHERE year(order_date) = 2025
GROUP BY product
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
plan.explanation: Adds up 2025 revenue for each product and keeps the ten with the most.

question: Which category has the highest profit margin?

plan.title: Profit margin by category
plan.sql:
SELECT category,
       round(sum(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue,
       round(sum(revenue) - sum(cost), 2) AS profit,
       round((sum(revenue) - sum(cost)) / sum(revenue), 4) AS profit_margin
FROM global_sales
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY profit_margin DESC
plan.explanation: For each category, subtracts cost from revenue to get profit, then divides profit by revenue to get the margin.
assumptions: Profit margin is (revenue - cost) / revenue over all years.

question: How does discount relate to units sold?

plan.title: Units per order by discount
plan.sql:
SELECT discount, round(avg(units), 2) AS avg_units, count(*) AS orders
FROM global_sales
GROUP BY discount
ORDER BY discount
plan.explanation: Groups orders by their discount and shows the average number of units per order at each discount level.
assumptions: Each discount level is compared on average units per order.

question: What share of revenue comes from each customer segment?

plan.title: Revenue share by customer segment
plan.sql:
SELECT customer_segment,
       round(sum(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue,
       round(sum(revenue) / sum(sum(revenue)) OVER (), 4) AS revenue_share
FROM global_sales
GROUP BY customer_segment
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
plan.explanation: Adds up revenue for each customer segment and divides it by total revenue to get each segment's share.
assumptions: revenue_share is a fraction: 0.6 means 60% of all revenue.

question: What is the return rate by category?
aliases: which category has the most returns

plan.title: Return rate by category
plan.sql:
SELECT category, round(avg(CASE WHEN returned THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 4) AS return_rate, count(*) AS orders
FROM global_sales
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY return_rate DESC
plan.explanation: For each category, divides the number of returned orders by the number of orders.
assumptions: return_rate is a fraction of orders: 0.09 means 9% were returned.

question: Revenue by country in APAC
aliases: which apac country has the most revenue

plan.title: APAC revenue by country
plan.sql:
SELECT country, round(sum(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM global_sales
WHERE region = 'APAC'
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
plan.explanation: Keeps orders from the APAC region and adds up revenue for each country.

question: What is the average order value by month?

plan.title: Average order value by month
plan.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS month, round(avg(revenue), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM global_sales
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY month
plan.explanation: Averages the revenue of the orders placed in each month.
assumptions: Each row is one order, so order value is the row's revenue.

plan.title: Total revenue, 2025
plan.sql:
SELECT round(sum(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM global_sales
WHERE year(order_date) = 2025
plan.explanation: Adds up the revenue of every order placed in 2025.
